Another VPN app is running, and Android only allows one at a time — so it switched Safe World off. Close that app, then turn protection back on. Turning on \'Always-on VPN\' below stops this happening again.

Android lets only one VPN run at a time, so another VPN app can switch Safe World off. Turning on \'Always-on VPN\' — and \'Block connections without VPN\' — makes Android start Safe World itself and refuse to pass traffic while it is off. This is the only way to stop that, and only you can turn it on.
In VPN settings, tap the gear next to Safe World, then turn on both switches.
Couldn\'t open VPN settings on this device.
Private DNS is blocking Safe World
Your phone is sending web lookups encrypted to another provider, where Safe World can\'t check them. Blocking will not work until Private DNS is set to Off or Automatic.

Blocking an app means Safe World has to check every connection your phone makes, not just website lookups. That uses more battery. Nothing is sent anywhere — all the checking happens on this phone.
